title: Signal Loupe Drillboard — correlated call-path exploration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Redwood Console needs a compact, developer-friendly workspace for deep investigation of individual LLM inference requests and their downstream call paths. Existing designs focus on long, linear visualizations; customers asked for a denser, pivotable canvas that surfaces linked events by ID, execution buckets, and resource cost without sacrificing the ability to step through the sequence.

Goal: Deliver a prototype 'Signal Loupe Drillboard' — a collapsible canvas that centers on a single correlation ID (signal ID) and shows: call-path lanes (service -> GPU host -> model shard), time-sliced execution bands, token-cost heatbars, and a micro-filter rail for quick narrowing. It should support keyboard-driven stepping, pinning of nodes, and in-context links to logs, trace artifacts, and rollout metadata.

Key UX principles:
- Minimal cognitive load: present dense information in readable micro-tiles rather than giant swimlanes.
- Contextual affordances: hover previews, inline cost badges, and single-key navigation to step forward/back.
- Actionable links: surface relevant runbooks, PRs, or rollouts tied to an event node.

User flows covered:
1) Investigate a slow request: start on a signal ID, inspect call-path lanes, identify a hotspot by cost heatbar, open the node to see kernel selection and batch details, then open the related rollout snapshot.
2) Compare two sibling signals: pin left/right panes, sync time window, toggle cost overlays to compare batching impact.
3) Emergency fallback audit: filter to last 50ms errors across lanes, export selected nodes to an incident timeline.

Prototype scope:
- Drillboard canvas with up to 6 horizontal lanes representing logical service boundaries.
- Compact event tiles with key metrics: duration, GPU, model-variant tag, token delta, cost estimate.
- Micro-filter rail (status, latency bucket, kernel tag, model family) with quick counts.
- Node detail flyout with links: Figma design spec, PRD, GitHub PR, and runtime metrics snapshot.
- Keyboard nav: J/K step between events, P to pin, E to expand a node.

Accessibility / performance constraints:
- Ensure color palette meets AA contrast for heatbars and badges.
- Limit initial DOM nodes; lazy-render lanes beyond viewport to preserve console responsiveness.

Dependencies and integrations:
- Needs runtime metrics endpoint from ENG (ENG-4521) that returns node-level kernel and batch metadata.
- Small backend contract for cost estimates (ENG-4607).
- Console tracing route to accept signal_id param (ENG-4672).

Acceptance criteria:
- Click-through prototype in Figma with working keyboard nav simulated.
- Usability test with 5 internal engineers: median task time to locate a hotspot <= 4 minutes.
- Instrumented console route returns expected payload shape and prototype renders without JS errors.
- Design handoff tokens and component specs checked in Figma, with a design review approval from PM and Eng.

Notes for reviewers:
- The prototype intentionally compresses event tiles to prioritize density; we expect feedback on readability vs density trade-offs.
- We experimented with showing direct kernel names; if security or IP concerns arise, we can mask to kernel-family strings (decision logged below).
comments: 2025-02-20 — Initial concept sketched during design sync. Diego volunteered to pair with Eng to align payload fields.
2025-02-25 — UX research: 3/5 engineers preferred the compact-tile approach; two asked for larger time ruler context. Added optional time-ruler overlay to prototype.
2025-02-28 — Eng review (Carla H.): backend can expose kernel tag and batch-size but not raw kernel version without separate security signoff (ENG-4607 blocked by security).
2025-03-01 — PM (Evan L.) asks for inclusion of rollout tag and canary status inline on pinned nodes — added to node detail flyout and small badge on event tiles.
2025-03-03 — Prototype updated in Figma (v3). Ready for design review. Attached a short video demo for reviewers.
2025-03-04 — Design review notes: tighten contrast on heatbars, add obvious affordance for 'open in logs', and consider an automatic grouping for repeated sub-requests.
decisions: Tile-first approach chosen over full swimlane to improve density for enterprise incident work.
Expose kernel-family vs raw kernel version in initial iteration to avoid security concerns; raw kernel versions may be gated behind an admin flag later.
Keyboard navigation (J/K) included to support power users and reduce mouse dependence for deep dives.
tradeoffs: Density vs readability: compressing event tiles reduces scrolling but can hide nuance; mitigations: expandable detail flyouts and optional time-ruler overlay.
Data surface area vs security: showing full kernel metadata is valuable for troubleshooting but constrained by IP/security policies — chosen to show aggregated family tags first.
Client-side rendering complexity vs console performance: lazy-render lanes beyond the viewport implemented to avoid large memory/paint costs.
